newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen, fighting SCI takeover, announces new buys.
newsitem.headline: Loewen, fighting SCI takeover, announces new buys.

text.p: The Loewen Group Inc announced on Sunday acquisitions which it said reflected concerns about the anticompetitive effects of the hostile takeover bid from Service Corp International (SCI).
SCI, North America's largest funeral home operator, launched a bid on September 17 to takeover Loewen, the second largest. Loewen said in a statement on Sunday that it

bought CMS West, a western-Pennsylvania-based operator of 28 cemeteries and seven funeral homes. The acquisition was made before the SCI bid but announced at a cemetery and funeral association convention in Florida that ended on Saturday.
It said it had now made nearly US$100 million of acquisitions in the past three weeks, some of them since the SCI bid.

"The acquisition interest we've seen in the last twelve days reflects serious concerns among potential sellers of funeral and cemetery properties about the negative impact SCI's proposed acquisition will have on the market," Loewen Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Raymond L. Loewen said.
"The anticompetitive effects of the proposed acquisition have already prompted regulatory scrutiny in several jurisdictions."

The company had on Friday publicized the fact that the state of Florida, where many senior citizens retire, had launched an investigation into potential anticompetitive effects of SCI's proposed acquisition.

Loewen asserted that sellers wanted to deal with it: "Loewen enjoys the best reputation in our industry. The superior quality of our people, our management and employees at all levels of our Company, has been the major driver of our success.

"In addition, our demonstrated record of caring for our employees, our customers and the communities that we serve has motivated potential sellers within the industry increasingly to deal with Loewen."

With offices in Vancouver, Cincinnati, and Philadelphia, Loewen employs over 13,000 people. Since the first of the year, it has closed or signed approximately US$715 million in acquisitions, not including the Rose Hills and Prime Succession transactions valued at over US$535 million.
More than 90 percent of the Company's revenue is generated in the United States, and its shares will be listed on the New York Stock Exchange on October 2.
